title: Containers Under the Hood
summary: What a container really is: ordinary Linux processes isolated by namespaces, limited by cgroups v2 and given their own root filesystem by overlayfs — plus the OCI specs and the CLI → dockerd → containerd → shim → runc chain that makes it happen.
objectives: Explain a container as a process with namespaces, cgroups, a layered root filesystem and reduced privileges
Name the seven namespace types Docker uses and what each isolates
Read cgroup v2 files (memory.max, cpu.max, pids.max, memory.events, cpu.stat) to understand limits and throttling
Describe how overlayfs layers, copy-on-write and whiteouts turn an image into a container filesystem
Describe the OCI image and runtime specs and the role of dockerd, containerd, the shim and runc
Compare containers and virtual machines, including their security trade-offs
